issue.title: Add case insensitivity feature to GenericFunction.
issue.body:
### Description
Fixes: #4569

Following this discussion: https://github.com/geoalchemy/geoalchemy2/pull/216
The goal of the PR is to allow the possibility to register case-insensitive `GenericFunction(s)`.
By default, the case-sensitivity is kept in order to keep the current behavior.

### Checklist
<!-- go over following points. check them with an `x` if they do apply, (they turn into clickable checkboxes once the PR is submitted, so no need to do everything at once)

-->

This pull request is:

- [ ] A documentation / typographical error fix
	- Good to go, no issue or tests are needed
- [ ] A short code fix
	- please include the issue number, and create an issue if none exists, which
	  must include a complete example of the issue.  one line code fixes without an
	  issue and demonstration will not be accepted.
	- Please include: `Fixes: #<issue number>` in the commit message
	- please include tests.   one line code fixes without tests will not be accepted.
- [x] A new feature implementation
	- please include the issue number, and create an issue if none exists, which must
	  include a complete example of how the feature would look.
	- Please include: `Fixes: #<issue number>` in the commit message
	- please include tests.

**Have a nice day!**

body: please review #4467 where the case sensitivity of generic functions is also discussed.  Changes ilke these are often very dangerous to merge in point releases as they can break backwards compatibility.   For example here what if someone has defined two GenericFunctions that differ only in case, what happens?  should that now raise an error?
My apologies, I missed the "case_sensitive=True" flag above.

however, my thinking is that this should be an across-the-board change.  I would prefer to target at 1.4 and make these names case insensitive across the board.    The PR is very well written but is too much complexity for something I think will not see enough use and it is possibly more likely that everyone would appreciate a more consistent case sensitivity story.

Thanks for these comments!

> For example here what if someone has defined two GenericFunctions that differ only in case, what happens? should that now raise an error?

If they are both defined with `case_sensitive = True`, which is the default behavior, they will coexist. But if they are defined with `case_sensitive = False`, the last one will overwrite the first one silently. I was thinking about raising a warning or an exception in this case but I realized that this behavior (the last one overriding the first one) already exists in the master branch if we define 2 functions with the same identifier, so I did not add warnings/exceptions in this case to be consistent with the current behavior (but we could add some).

> however, my thinking is that this should be an across-the-board change. I would prefer to target at 1.4 and make these names case insensitive across the board. The PR is very well written but is too much complexity for something I think will not see enough use and it is possibly more likely that everyone would appreciate a more consistent case sensitivity story.

I agree that the more consistent the better.
But the current implementation is quite bug-prone and these bugs are quite hard to understand (e.g. when the query returns something but not with the expected type, the crash can occur much later after the actual bug (it actually happened to someone in my team, he spent a full day to find that a 't' should have been a 'T' :smile: , that's why I am here)). So I still think that something should be done about it.
But maybe we could use another temporary strategy? E.g. allowing a `force_case_sensitivity` attribute to the `GenericFunction` that would raise an exception when one call a function that is not registered and that another one is registered with the same lowercase name which has the `force_case_sensitivity` attribute set to `True`. But I am not fond of it.

There's another way, which is to change it to work case insensitively, but detect when someone has created two generic functions that name-conflict on different cases, then emit a warning, then support both of those in a deprecated "case sensitive" mode.    This is a little more intricate to implement and also we always add test for deprecated behaviors in the corresponding "test_deprecations.py" test suite, in this case test/sql/test_deprecations.py.

So this reduces the scope of backwards compatibility.  There is still the chance of backwards incompatibility in that if an application is calling one of their functions using the wrong casing, and is getting an object back that "works" because their GenericFunction in fact doesn't work (like datatypes or something), that would suddenly be exposed.  That is, it's exactly the bug you found but in reverse.  But this is such an unlikely situation it's not worth worrying about.

I have a few ideas on the implementation too, as I like to minimize "deprecated" codepaths as much as possible, but lets get the basic behavioral contract and tests happening first and I can refine it after that.

Indeed, this way would be better but I was afraid of introducing backward incompatibilities in the libraries depending on sqlalchemy. But if you think it is ok let's go for it!
Should I close #4570 then?
you can force-push to it a new revision if you'd like, i have no cycles to write new code in the near term...
Ok, I will try to take some time for this in the next few days.

I pushed a new commit in #4570 that should work as you described.
I did not move any test to `test/sql/test_deprecations.py` for now, I will clean this up later if we agree on the functional part.
Also, I had to rework the test `test/sql/test_functions.py::CompileTest::test_uppercase` because a `GenericFunction` with an identifier `now` is already registered when executing this test. But as I don't know the actual purpose of this test, it might be an unwanted change.

**Adrien Berchet** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**Add case insensitivity feature to GenericFunction.** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/1178

issue.title: quoted name is not applied to function name even when specified

labels.name: use case
labels.description: not really a feature or a bug; can be support for new DB features or user use cases not anticipated

issue.body:
There is one error when moving from 1.2.8 to 1.3.12 version.

I defined custom GenericFunction like this:

```python
class CustomFunction(GenericFunction): 
      type = Boolean 
      package = 'pack' 
      name = '"CustomFunction"' 
      identifier = 'CustomFunction'
```

When I used it with 1.2.8 version all was right, but when I use it
with 1.3.12 I get this error:
```postgresql
function "CustomFunction"(bigint) does not exist
```

I look at generated sql code and see following:

```postgresql
 SELECT ...,  """CustomFunction"""("columnName")  \nFROM ...
```

SQLAlchemy quotes already quoted name. I tried to find the reasons of this behaviour
and it seems it's in the `compiler.py` module. In particular, in the methods `requires_quotes` and `quote_identifier` of `IdentifierPreparer` class. They don't check if the name already has quotes.

In situation when name is without quotes, but in camel case, it converts name to lower case.

P.S. I use that GenericFunction definition when I need to construct dynamic query which
should contain calling of stored procedure in `select` section. For example:

```python
...
query = select([ 
    Table.c.column, 
    func.pack.CustomFunction(Table.c.column) ])

# code with conditions for adding relevant where clauses, like
# if condition:
#    query = query.where(...) 
...
``` 

Best regards.
